title: Listeria and food safety during pregnancy
summary: Pregnant people should avoid unpasteurized dairy products and heat higher-risk ready-to-eat foods, including deli meats, until steaming hot.

title: Advice about eating fish
summary: People who are pregnant should choose lower-mercury fish and eat 2 to 3 servings a week from the Best Choices list while avoiding fish with the highest mercury levels.

title: Foods to avoid in pregnancy
summary: Guidance covers pasteurization, raw or undercooked animal products, certain fish, caffeine, and washing produce during pregnancy.

title: Nutrition During Pregnancy
organization: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists
summary: A varied diet during pregnancy should include protein, iron, folic acid, calcium, vitamin D, choline, and omega-3 fatty acids; individual needs should be discussed with a clinician.

title: Moderate Caffeine Consumption During Pregnancy
organization: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists
summary: Moderate caffeine consumption below 200 mg per day does not appear to be a major contributing factor in miscarriage or preterm birth; total intake across sources matters.

title: Safer Food Choices for Pregnant People
organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
summary: Pregnancy increases the risk from some foodborne illnesses. Safer choices include pasteurized dairy and thoroughly cooked meat, eggs, seafood, and sprouts.
